messages:
maria_cs: Hey team — customer ACME reported ~20 users were provisioned from Okta but none of them have any roles assigned in Redwood. They can log in, but see no org/team access. Reported ~10:45am PT.

devon_se: thanks, any quick screenshots or csv? do we have a repro org id?

maria_cs: org_id=org_0acme123, sent a redacted csv in DM showing users present in Users list but empty `roles` column. Okta SCIM app is the managed connector, name `ACME - Redwood`.

samir_idp: grabbing SCIM logs now. I see PATCH /Groups/<id> and POST /Users, but role assignment path (we expect role mapping via group->role webhook) returns 403 from our auth layer. Error in our logs: `403 token_missing_scope: insufficient_scope for groups:write`.

elsa_support: picture of the 403?

samir_idp: pasted snippet from prod logs:```
[2026-03-14T17:45:23Z] request_id=req_8f3a PATCH /api/scim/v2/Groups/00gabc123 status=403 body={"detail":"insufficient_scope","error":"token_missing_scope","allowed_scopes":["scim:groups:write","scim:users:write"]}
```

maria_cs: customer claims they used the default Okta SCIM token created by their admin wizard. Could it be Okta not sending full scopes?

samir_idp: looked at token metadata — the token attached to ACME's SCIM app only has `scim:users:write` scope. No groups scope. That explains 403 when our service tries to update group membership -> which is how we map groups to roles.

devon_se: ah — that would result in users created but never added to groups, and we only map roles from groups. can we confirm group name/externalId mapping wasn't the issue too?

samir_idp: checked a few `POST /api/scim/v2/Users` payloads. They contain `groups: []` in the body because Okta is not writing group membership on user create without group write scope. Example payload we saw:```
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],
  "userName": "jane.doe@acme.com",
  "name": {"givenName":"Jane","familyName":"Doe"},
  "emails": [{"value":"jane.doe@acme.com","primary":true}],
  "groups": []
}
```

maria_cs: customer says they did have groups in Okta and expected them to map. Okta docs say group push needs both `scim.groups:write` and admin has to enable `Push Groups` — could be they missed toggle.

elsa_support: timeline: they enabled SCIM on Friday, saw users appear on Friday, then roles missing Monday. Could be token update/regen over weekend.

devon_se: short-term workaround: we can run a one-off recon job that reads Okta group membership via their API (if they grant us an Okta admin token) or they can re-provision by enabling group push and re-sync. For safety, we should not auto-assign roles until groups are confirmed.

samir_idp: recommended fix message to send to customer (draft):
- Confirm `Push Groups` is enabled in Okta app integration.
- Ensure SCIM token has `scim:groups:write` scope (Okta calls these `Group Push` permissions).
- If they regenerate the token, do a full group sync: in Redwood Console -> Integrations -> SCIM -> "Resync groups" (or we can trigger from our side).

maria_cs: sending draft to customer. Also asked if they want us to run manual reconciliation.

customer_reply (pasted by maria_cs): "We regenerated the token last night when rotating creds. We thought rotating would keep perms. We didn't toggle any new settings. Please reassign roles — >200 users affected."

devon_se: rotation likely created a token with default narrower scope. Okta's token wizard sometimes requires explicitly enabling group push.

elsa_support: can we do a safe reconciliation script? I can run a scoped job that only creates GroupMember links (no role changes) to avoid accidentally escalating. We need okta org admin API key from customer or they can turn on the push.

samir_idp: here's a quick curl to validate token scopes against our SCIM introspect endpoint:```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.inference/v1/scim/introspect
# returns: {"token":"valid","scopes":["scim:users:write"]}
```

devon_se: good. ops question: if we run a one-off that adds group members based on Okta exports, we must also emit audit logs and not touch role assignments beyond mapping existing group->role mapping already configured. I'll own the job. tagging @eng-identity for code review if needed.

eng-identity-bot: Automated note: create a PR checklist for reconciliation job: unit tests, audit events, idempotency, rate-limit handling.

maria_cs: customer provided Okta admin API key (redacted). I've uploaded to vault in the `scim-acme` secret. Please proceed when ready.

devon_se: plan: (1) run a dry-run export compare (list groups from Okta, list members from Redwood), (2) produce delta, (3) run apply for members only. Timeline: try to run dry-run today EOD. I'll post results here.

samir_idp: one more gotcha we saw on a different tenant: Okta truncates long group names and adds `...` which broke our external_id matching. For ACME, internal group externalIds look fine. If any mismatches show up in dry-run, we should prefer matching on canonical email lists and fallback to name similarity.

elsa_support: customer asked if we can prevent this in future — recommend they enable automated token policy that preserves scopes on rotation and use service token with explicit scopes rather than ephemeral wizard token.

maria_cs: I sent the instructions and asked them to keep their console open while we run the dry-run. I'll update once devon posts results. :thumbsup:

devon_se: dry-run complete: found 196 missing group-memberships across 12 groups. sample delta: `group Billing-Team` missing 48, `group Data-Platform` missing 65. Pushing reconcile in 30m (no role changes beyond mapping).

samir_idp: monitoring logs during reconcile. I'll watch for 403s. If we hit token scope error, we'll stop the job.

devon_se: reconcile finished — 0 errors, audit events emitted, members added. Customer confirmed roles appear and users now have expected access.

maria_cs: closing loop with ACME. Action items:
- customer to use dedicated SCIM service token with `scim:users:write` and `scim:groups:write` and enable Push Groups in Okta.
- we (eng-identity) to add an error message in SCIM onboarding UI that warns when token scope is missing `scim:groups:write`.
- ops: reconciliation runbook added to customer-success wiki.

elsa_support: thanks all. leaving notes in the case and tagging for postmortem doc. :white_check_mark:

maria_cs: marking resolved for now, will reopen if customer sees regressions.
